summary: Mandatory professional framing can introduce authority bias, brittle refusals, and narrower reasoning without adding knowledge.

points.text: An invented credential or seniority cue can cause users to over-trust an answer and reviewers to miss unsupported claims, especially when the model produces polished professional language.
A narrow professional identity can anchor the model to one discipline's default solution and suppress cross-domain alternatives or legitimate uncertainty.

Generic instructions to refuse when unsure do not produce calibrated uncertainty. Models may refuse answerable cases or answer unanswerable ones unless the behavior is tested on representative examples.
Long persona prompts compete with task evidence and can conflict with higher-priority policy or user needs. The same tokens may be better spent on source context, examples, and acceptance criteria.
